Sessions named for what you typed, not for a colour

Wortel 2026.44.2 · 2026-10-27

No more sessions named after a colour. When Claude Code starts, it asks the terminal what colour its background is, and the answer travels to Claude down the same path as your typing. Wortel reads that path to name a session from your first prompt, and it took the answer for something you had typed. Pressing Return at the folder trust question was enough to send it off as your “prompt”, and the session came out as “Extract hex color values” or “Decode hex color code”. Wortel now tells the terminal’s answers apart from your keys, so the name comes from what you actually asked.

Esc is just Esc. After pressing Esc twice to clear Claude’s input, the first letter you typed next could go missing from the session’s name. It no longer does. A single Esc followed by an arrow or another key is no longer mistaken for Esc Esc either.

Change Directory waits for you, not for the terminal. A move waiting for the agent to go quiet now holds off while you type, paste, click or scroll in that session, and no longer mistakes the terminal’s answers to the agent for someone typing.

A worktree sheet again, and servers in your own browser

Wortel 2026.44.1 · 2026-10-27

New Worktree Session has its sheet back. ⇧⌘N opens one small form: the branch, the branch it starts from, and the folder the worktree goes in. A name is already filled in and selected, so pressing Return makes the session straight away, as before, and that name is replaced with one that fits the work once the session has a name. Type your own to name the branch yourself. Location shows where this repository’s worktrees go and changes it for the next ones too, the same setting as Worktree Location… in the folder menu.

Open servers in your browser. A server in the running-jobs list opened in a tab inside Wortel. Turn on Open Servers in Default Browser in the View menu, or Always Open in Browser on a server’s right-click menu, and a click sends it to Chrome, Safari or whichever browser is your default. The menu still offers both, for the times you want the other one.

Tab previews in dark mode. The preview card you get when you rest on a tab kept a white background after switching to dark mode, with the terminal’s grey text on it barely readable. It now follows the appearance, the box and its edges both.

Move a session to another folder

Wortel 2026.43.3 · 2026-10-23

Move a session, agent and all. You ask Claude to start a new project next door, it makes the folder and keeps working there, and the session, its Git panel and its sidebar folder stay behind on the old project. Change Directory in the session menu, or wortel cd <folder> from inside the session, now moves it. The shell changes to the new folder, keeping its scrollback, and Claude picks up the same conversation there. The session is filed under that folder in the sidebar (a new folder if none covers it, the way Open Folder makes one), and the Git panel and Files follow.

It waits for the right moment. A move never cuts Claude off. It happens once the turn has ended, not while Claude waits on a permission or a question, and not while you’re typing into its box. Until then the session’s row says where it’s going. Claude can ask for the move itself, and Wortel tells it straight away what will happen, including any background task that will stop. Run the command again with another folder to change the destination, or with the folder you’re in to call it off.

Claude Code is the agent that can move today. Other agents, and a program running in the foreground like an editor or a dev server, are refused with a reason rather than interrupted.
